DISCLOSURE: this PASS originally (pre-2026-09-01-fix) rested only on the single happy-path injected_failure_stage='post_mutation' string. An independent coordinator review found that any OTHER truthy injected_failure_stage value fell through apply_transaction's two known branches, still reached the real mutating write, then raised on record_attempt's synthetic-SUCCEEDED guard -- and the bare `except PortableReleaseTransactionError: raise` re-raised WITHOUT restoring, leaving disk mutated while lineage still claimed the old generation (torn state). Classified PRODUCT_NEGATIVE, see blockers.json. FIX (same-day): (1) a case-insensitive whitelist (KNOWN_INJECTED_FAILURE_STAGES={'pre_mutation','post_mutation'}) now rejects any unrecognized injected_failure_stage before any plan is built or mutation attempted; (2) the post-mutation recovery path now restores the exact predecessor snapshot and verifies the restored digest equals plan.source_state_sha256 before re-raising, for both apply_transaction and the previously-unguarded apply_rollback. Post-fix: P6's happy-path digest chain is unchanged and re-verified in this same re-run (predecessor/observed/fresh-on-disk all identical, 68513b5bcff37c9d120033d8084e7855fafd98c69590df25011f8a917c840a61, generation still 1). Three new regression tests prove the hardened path directly: an unknown stage string is rejected pre-mutation with disk/lineage byte-for-byte unchanged; the coordinator's exact repro string 'POST_MUTATION' is shown to normalize to the known 'post_mutation' alias and complete a clean ROLLED_BACK receipt (no exception, no torn state -- stronger than raise-then-recover); and a genuinely-unknown stage forced past the whitelist is shown to restore disk to plan.source_state_sha256 before the exception propagates. All three were confirmed to genuinely FAIL against the pre-fix code (via git stash of only the fix, keeping the new tests) and genuinely PASS against the fixed code.

For the success path, P7 re-entered from a genuinely fresh python3 subprocess (not in-process) after the P5 UPDATE and its independent_readback matched the persisted lineage exactly (generation 1, same state digest). For the explicit-ROLLBACK path, predecessor-byte restoration and new-generation minting are proven only in-process by the unit test, not yet by a fresh cross-process readback in this run -- that asymmetry is a known gap, not a silent overclaim. DISCLOSURE: the earlier PASS additionally rested on an unstated assumption that every raised-and-recovered path leaves disk consistent with lineage before a later reader (in-process or cross-process, e.g. P7's independent_readback) can observe it. The coordinator's PRODUCT_NEGATIVE finding (see H3, blockers.json) showed this was false for any injected_failure_stage string outside the one tested happy path: disk could be left mutated while lineage still claimed the old generation, which a subsequent readback (in-process or cross-process) would then either read as silently torn or fail to reconcile. The same-day fix (case-insensitive stage whitelist rejected before mutation; post-mutation recovery-then-verify-then-reraise for both apply_transaction and apply_rollback) closes this for every reader, not just the one gate that happened to be exercised. No duplicate irreversible effects were possible or observed: managed_dir is pure local filesystem state with no network/external calls in the wrapped seam (see H12).

P8 declared a forged target_release digest that did not match the actual payload bytes. apply_transaction raised SelfUpdateTransactionError('hostile-twin rejected before mutation: ...') before any filesystem write; on-disk digest before/after the attempt was identical and generation stayed at 1.

Every in-process gate (P5 install/update, P6 rollback, P8, P9, P10) recorded real, non-fabricated wall-time, resource.getrusage CPU, RSS and /proc/self/io disk deltas in measurements.jsonl. All are bounded, sub-second, and on the order of tens of milliseconds for the recovery path (freshly re-measured 2026-09-01 against the fixed code: rollback_duration_ms=27.3516190063674, failure_detection_ms=66.5779149858281). Numbers moved slightly from the pre-fix run's 25.6894439808093/62.00227601220831 because the recovery path now does additional restore-and-verify work (see H3); still tens of milliseconds, same order of magnitude. Caveat: measured against the 62M curated sandbox, not the full ~5G real ~/.claude tree; no extrapolation to full size was performed (would be invented, not measured).

This run never touches the real, running Claude Code instance or its actual cognition/agent-loop behavior -- that is Phase 13 and explicitly out of scope for SELFINT-20260901-a1c9e2f4. No pre/post-integration behavioral baseline of the live primary Frankenstein was captured, and none should be captured from a sandboxed self-integration run. Requires a live-integration run (Phase 13) under independent review before this can be assessed.

P9 replayed an UPDATE whose target equals the already-active release; rejected with 'UPDATE target must differ from active release', state and generation unchanged (rejected_no_double_apply=true). The unit test additionally covers the CAS-stale-replay variant (same payload, stale expected_generation) and gets the analogous fail-closed rejection. Neither path double-applies or diverges state.

P10: caller B advanced the lineage to generation 2 successfully; caller A, holding a stale expected_generation/expected_state_sha256 belief, was rejected fail-closed ('expected generation does not match current lineage'). Final state is exactly caller B's; no_split_brain=true.

This is a process/governance claim, not a runtime-gate claim: all evidence produced by this run was written exclusively to the non-canonical evidence_inbox path, no canonical workpackages/ file was mutated, and canonicalization_proposal.json explicitly marks status PROPOSAL_ONLY_ZERO_ACCEPTANCE_CREDIT with requested_independent_review=true. No artifact in this run asserts its own acceptance.

Only 2 of the 5 named phases have a directly measured, non-fabricated timing in this run: failure_detection_ms=66.5779149858281 and rollback_duration_ms=27.3516190063674, both from the P6 gate, freshly re-measured 2026-09-01 against the fixed (harder-working, restore-and-verify) recovery path -- moved slightly from the pre-fix run's 62.00227601220831/25.6894439808093 for that reason, still the same order of magnitude. 'process re-entry' and 'healthy readback' are demonstrated qualitatively and cross-process by P7, but P7 was run after the P5 success path, not chained immediately after the P6 rollback recovery as a single continuously-timed sequence. A single run that times all five phases detection->rollback begin->rollback end->re-entry->readback back-to-back has not been produced; reporting a full decomposition would require inventing missing timings, which is disallowed.

The wrapped seam (self_update_transaction.py) performs only local filesystem reads/writes/snapshots under managed_dir/control_dir; it makes no network calls and fires no external side effects. All injected failures (pre_mutation, post_mutation) are local-filesystem-only. No artifact in this run claims or implies that local rollback constitutes rollback of any external/irreversible effect; integration_map.json's irreversible_effect_boundaries list is empty for this run's actual selected seam.

Whether repaired G10 portable transaction source requires wholly fresh runtime-integration evidence versus inheriting G9 acceptance credit is a canonicalization/governance decision for independent reviewers, not something the P5-P11 gates executed in this sandboxed run can adjudicate. This run supplies fresh candidate evidence (per H10) but does not itself decide the credit-inheritance question.
